reasoning_traces.think:
The core epistemic structure emerges from the interplay between belief and reality. The first primitive establishes belief as a distinct psychic act—distinct from mere proposition—whereby a mind evaluates whether a proposition corresponds to reality. This leads to a fourfold structure: subject, predicate, relation, and belief attitude. The second primitive introduces a minimal cognitive system where a hallucinatory candle defines the entire universe of experience, demonstrating that belief arises even without external validation. The third primitive formalizes the distinction between hallucination and reality, introducing a decision boundary that determines belief validity. These primitives together suggest a dual-process model: one where belief is formed within a closed perceptual loop, and another where belief is validated against an external referent. Failure modes occur when the perceptual loop becomes self-referential or when the decision boundary collapses into ambiguity.
